title: Marker-keyed de-interleaving of two stacked sheets reveals an abstract symbol
question: The picture shows one framed lattice of 14 rows and 7 columns of square cells; each cell is either dark (filled) or blank. Beside every lattice row, just outside the frame on its left, exactly one marker is printed: either a filled dot or a hollow ring. Exactly 7 rows carry a filled dot and exactly 7 rows carry a hollow ring. Discard every row whose marker is a hollow ring, keep the rows whose marker is a filled dot in their original top-to-bottom order, and push those 7 kept rows together into a single block of 7 rows and 7 columns. The dark cells of that block form one of these five symbols: ring (a closed square outline with a hollow centre), wedge (a solid triangle pointing down, widest across its top row), zigzag (a bar along the top, a staircase running down to the left, and a bar along the bottom), arrow (a broad arrowhead pointing down with a short stem below it), slash (a thick diagonal band running from the top left corner to the bottom right corner). Which of the five symbols do the dark cells of that block form? Answer with one word.

task_signature.mechanism: Two 7x7 sheets of dark cells are shuffled together into one printed 14x7 lattice, and the only statement of which sheet a lattice row belongs to is the filled-dot or hollow-ring marker printed beside that row. The answer-bearing sheet exists in no contiguous region of the raster: the viewer must select the seven dot-marked rows, discard the seven interleaved ring-marked rows that carry a different decoy symbol drawn with the same number of dark cells, close the vertical gaps left behind, and only then match the compacted block to the nearest of five named symbol templates by Hamming distance.

latent_z.description: Latent scene: the printed lattice rows as fill glyphs, the per-row marker codes whose parity selects the sheet, the palette index, and the lattice placement jitter.

latent_alias.justification: Only the parity of each marker code is rendered and read, so adding two to every marker code is an exact alias; a filled cell is written with either of two interchangeable fill glyphs, so swapping those glyphs is a second exact alias. Both transforms render pixel-identically and leave the analytic gold unchanged, and latent_symmetries exercises both.

boundary.observable: Every quantity the decision depends on is printed: each lattice cell's fill and each row's dot-or-ring marker. The decision boundary is the visible event where the compacted seven-row block moves closer, cell for cell, to a competing named symbol than to the intended one, and near-boundary scenes are generated by moving cells along the difference set between the two closest templates.
boundary.quarantine: Scenes whose runner-up template gap is below two cells are flagged quarantined and excluded from headline claims, because at that separation a single misread cell flips the named symbol; the pixel arm independently abstains when the frame fiducial, the marker column, or the seven-versus-seven marker split is unreadable.

semantic_contrast.contrast: The nearest known world realigns every row of a single grid horizontally against its own bright anchor, so all printed ink survives and only the column index of each cell changes; the nearest negative serialises one grid and re-lays it at a different row length, so all printed ink survives and the reading order changes. Here nothing is shifted or reordered: two complete symbols occupy the same lattice at once, and the operation is a marker-keyed subset selection followed by vertical compaction that deletes half the printed ink. The discarded sheet is a different symbol carrying the same number of dark cells, so total ink, column histograms, and every local neighbourhood are shared by both answers and only the dot-versus-ring binding decides which symbol is reported.
semantic_contrast.expected_information_gain: Isolates whether a model can bind a per-row categorical fiducial to lattice rows, filter a two-dimensional figure down to the marked subset while ignoring an equally salient interleaved decoy figure, and close the resulting gaps before holistic shape identification.
